title: Physics-Based versus Data-Driven Classification of Single-Photon Quantum Emitters from Sparse Autocorrelation Data
summary: Identifying single photon emitters from large, inhomogeneous candidate populations is key to realizing many quantum applications. This requires measuring the emitters second order autocorrelation function, whose statistical reliability is fundamentally limited by acquisition time. Machine learning classifiers can accelerate identification from sparse data, but their performance relative to physics-based inference has not been systematically examined. Here, we introduce sequential Bayesian inference for single photon emitter classification and benchmark it against Levenberg-Marquardt fitting…
